answer: An agent marketplace trading umber pigment, garden tools, and prism lenses weights each agent’s vote by the collateral it locks for 90 days, with no bonus for having a separate identity. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agents still buys only 100 tokens of voting weight. To control a majority, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more collateral than all honest voters combined, tying up capital for the full lock period.
